note: What a total loss settlement must include besides the car's value. First-party = your own insurer; third-party = the at-fault driver's insurer.

sources.label: Matthiesen, Wickert & Lehrer, Payment of Sales Tax After Vehicle Total Loss in All 50 States (updated January 21, 2026)

AL.note: Cash settlements must include all applicable taxes, license fees and other fees.

AK.note: No state sales tax, but local taxes, license and transfer fees for a comparable car are owed, also if you keep the salvage.

AZ.note: Cash settlement must include all applicable taxes, license fees and other fees; same rule for third-party claims.

AR.note: Cash settlement must include taxes, license fees and other fees, itemised; same rule for third-party claims.

CA.note: Cash settlement on the cost of a comparable car including all applicable taxes and fees; third-party total losses are evaluated the same way. Part of the vehicle license fee is refundable from the DMV.

CO.note: Insurers must pay title fees, sales tax and any other transfer or registration fee; applies to third-party claims too.

CT.note: When the insurer takes title, it adds sales tax at the current rate to the settlement.

DE.note: No state sales tax and no rule on fees; check your policy wording.

DC.note: No statute, regulation or case on tax or fees; check your policy wording.

FL.note: Settlement must include sales tax, itemised separately from the car's value; same rule for third-party claims.

GA.note: Cash settlement must include all applicable taxes and other fees.

HI.note: Excise tax and ownership fees are repaid if you buy a replacement within 30 days of a cash settlement.

ID.note: No statute or rule, but the Department of Insurance says you can recover sales tax, title fees and release-of-liability fees.
ID.citation: Idaho Department of Insurance consumer guidance

IL.note: If you buy or lease a replacement within 30 days of the settlement, the insurer pays sales tax, transfer and title fees on up to the total-loss value.

IN.note: Sales tax must be paid with the settlement, not only after you buy a replacement; the Department applies this to third-party claims too.

IA.note: Cash settlement on a comparable car must include all applicable taxes, license fees and other fees.

KS.note: Cash settlement must include all taxes, license fees and transfer fees, for all total loss claims.

KY.note: Cash settlement must include all applicable taxes, license fees and other fees; the regulation covers third-party claimants too.

LA.note: Courts split on first-party claims (no tax under an "actual cash value" policy in Clark v. Clarendon, 2003; tax and fees included where ACV is undefined in Cummings v. Allstate, M.D. La. 2023). Against the at-fault driver, damages include sales tax by statute.

ME.note: Policies must cover the sales tax credit you would have had trading the car in at the highest book value.

MD.note: Cash settlement on a substantially similar car must include all applicable taxes and transfer fees; third-party settlements too.

MA.note: The insurer owes the actual cash value on the day of the loss; no rule adds tax or fees.

MI.note: No statute, rule or case on tax or fees; check your policy wording. Claims against the at-fault driver are limited to the $3,000 mini-tort.

MN.note: Cash settlement on a comparable car must include all applicable taxes, license fees and other fees.

MS.note: Insurers must pay sales tax, title and license fees unless the policy clearly excludes them; the Department applies this to third-party claims.

MO.note: No requirement unless the policy says so; you can ask the state Department of Revenue for a sales tax refund instead.
MO.citation: Missouri Department of Insurance auto claim guide

MT.note: No state sales tax and no rule on fees; the insurer owes the car's cash value before the accident.

NE.note: Insurers must pay sales tax to put you back where you were; same for third-party claims.

NV.note: Cash settlement on a comparable car must include all applicable taxes and other fees.

NH.note: No state sales tax and no rule on fees.

NJ.note: Settlement is the value of a substantially similar car plus sales tax; the rule applies to third-party claims once liability is reasonably clear.

NM.note: No statute or rule, but the state regulator says the insurer must repay excise tax, title and registration charges after a cash settlement.

NY.note: Sales tax is added to the car's value; insurers don't have to pay transfer or title fees. Third-party total losses follow the same minimum-offer rules.

NC.note: No statute, rule or case on tax or fees; check your policy wording.

ND.note: No rule; the payment is the actual cash value less your deductible.

OH.note: If you buy a replacement within 30 days of a cash settlement, the insurer repays the sales tax, up to the tax on a car worth the settlement amount. Same rules for third-party claimants.

OK.note: Cash settlement on a comparable car must include all applicable taxes, license fees and other fees.

OR.note: No state sales tax, but license and other fees must be included, for third-party claims too.

PA.note: Settlement is the car's pre-loss fair market value plus sales tax on a replacement.

RI.note: Cash settlement must include all applicable taxes, license fees and other fees; the rule's "claimant" includes third parties.

SC.note: Not owed unless the policy says so (Schulmeyer v. State Farm, 2003). South Carolina charges a capped Infrastructure Maintenance Fee instead of sales tax.

SD.note: First-party depends on the policy; the regulator says sales tax is generally payable on third-party total losses.

TN.note: Sales tax on the car's value at the time of loss is owed on all total losses, including third-party claims, whether or not you replace the car (not leased cars).

TX.note: No rule requires it; under an "actual cash value" policy, taxes and fees aren't part of the value (Singleton v. Elephant Ins. Co., 5th Cir. 2020).

UT.note: Cash settlement must include all applicable taxes, license fees and other fees; same for third-party claims.

VT.note: Cash settlement must include all applicable taxes, license fees and other fees; same for third-party claims.

VA.note: Cash settlement must include all applicable taxes, license fees and other fees; insurers have been cited for paying them late.

WA.note: Settlement must include taxes and fees (pro-rated where annual), for third-party claims too, whether or not you keep the car.

WV.note: A cash settlement adds 5% of the car's value for the excise tax; same for third-party claims.
WV.citation: W. Va. Code § 33-6-33; W. Va. Code R. 114-14-7

WI.note: No specific rule, but the insurance commissioner has cited insurers for not paying sales tax on total losses.

WY.note: No law, but the Department of Insurance's position is that sales tax on the car's value is included.
